# What's a Good Way to Schedule Planting and Harvest Crews?


A good way is to create a schedule where each field operation is a task with date, crew, machines, and expected area, and to view all assignments on a shared calendar so conflicts and idle resources can be seen before the day starts. On **Jestor** , this runs through **Tasks** , crews and machines **tables** , and a calendar view.


Planting and harvest depend on timing and coordination. If crews and machines are assigned verbally, conflicts appear on the day, and good weather windows may be wasted while people and equipment wait.


## What informal crew scheduling costs


- Crews and machines assigned to two places at once
- Idle time while waiting for instructions
- Good weather windows lost
- Tasks done in the wrong order
- Little record of who worked where


## How crew scheduling works


- Each operation is a **task** with field, date, crew, and machines
- A calendar shows assignments for the whole farm
- Conflicts and idle resources are highlighted
- Crews receive their plan through a message


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Resources are used more fully during critical windows
- Crews know what to do before they arrive
- Managers can adjust plans quickly when conditions change
- This scales from a small farm to a large operation with many crews


Crews assigned verbally Crews and machines on a shared calendar


Conflicts and idle time Planned, visible, and adjustable


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can crew leaders receive the plan on their phones?** Yes, through WhatsApp or the platform. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can I reassign resources when the weather changes?** Yes, tasks and assignments can be edited at any time.


**Can I see machine availability?** Yes, a machines table can show status and maintenance.
